title: Spells and Magical Items
audit_comment: CHAPTER 3 of the DMO (printed pp. 68-85), the magic-management chapter closing in one round: the daily recovery doctrine (the eight-hour rest minimum, the 10 minutes per spell level, the eight-hour study cap, the no-sleep once-a-day rule, the restart on distraction), the wizard clarifications (the damage caps of horrid wilting, cone of cold and delayed blast fireball, the antimagic-shell scope, the ESP save ladder, the feather-fall bands, the fly maneuvering, the haste aging, the identify cost, the limited-wish and wish aging grids and scopes, the permanency and dispel doctrines, the teleport firm-surface rule and the permanent dimensions, the astral projection economics, the stoneskin limits), the priest clarifications (the holy-might cap, the know-time estimator, the plane-shift companions and the planar-research grid with the pocket-dimension modifiers, the nap and sentinel windows, the speak-with-dead range), and the item doctrines (the amulet seven days, the bag-of-holding air and water grid, the extradimensional seam, the potion 12th-level bar, the rod and staff rules, the sphere 92-percent control cap, the withering limb ladders, the stone of luck).

banner.title: SPELLS AND MAGICAL ITEMS - DMO Chapter 3 closes: the daily recovery doctrine (the good night's sleep and the eight-hour minimum, the ten minutes a level, the distraction restart, the eight-hour study cap), the wizard and priest per-spell clarifications (the antimagic-shell scope, the ESP save ladder, the haste aging, the identify cost, the wish framework with its race aging grids, the teleport and astral economics, the plane-shift rods with the research grid), and the item doctrines (the amulet window, the bag grid, the extradimensional seam with the portable-hole gate, the potion bar, the sphere cap, the withering ladders).
banner.provenance: verified against printed pp. 68-85 of the uploaded DMO session capture (part 1, printed page N at OCR page N+1); the Rozmare examples from pp. 69, 72 and 74, the permanency rosters from p. 73, the planar-research table from p. 79, the bag-of-holding table from p. 80, the item doctrines from pp. 79-85. The horrid-wilting die prints 16d8; the OCR B is a misread and the pin carries the note.
banner.sentinel: the gap census after this round: 42 closed, 54 open - Chapter 3 is DONE in one round per the advisory-prose scope ruling; the DMO arc continues with Chapter 4 (Creating Magical Items, pp. 86-95).

consts.name: deqRaceCount
consts.comment: the aging-ladder race count: five races, the human, the halfling and half-elf band, the dwarf, the gnome, the elf (printed pp. 72 and 76).

consts.name: deqPlaneTypeCount
consts.comment: the planar-research plane-type count: the inner, outer, demiplane and prime-material rows of the research table (printed p. 79).

consts.name: deqBagTypeCount
consts.comment: the bag-of-holding size count: the 250, 500, 1,000 and 1,500-pound bags (printed p. 80).

consts.name: deqMemorizeMinutesPerLevel
consts.comment: the memorization effort: 10 minutes of study per level of the spell (printed p. 68; the Rozmare fly spell at 3rd level takes 30 minutes).

consts.name: deqRestHoursMin
consts.comment: the rest requirement: about eight hours spent in reasonable comfort - never a night in a saddle - is the minimum to regain spells (printed p. 68).

consts.name: deqStudyHoursMax
consts.comment: the limited-study cap: a spellcaster can spend a maximum of eight hours a day acquiring spells; past that no concentration remains, with no other disadvantage (printed p. 69).

consts.name: deqHorridWiltingDice
consts.comment: the horrid-wilting cap, the die count: the maximum damage is 16 dice (printed p. 69; the OCR renders the die as 16dB, read as 16d8).

consts.name: deqHorridWiltingDieSize
consts.comment: the horrid-wilting cap, the die: d8 (printed p. 69, the OCR B misread).

consts.name: deqConeOfColdDice
consts.comment: the cone-of-cold maximum damage, the die count: 10d4+10 points (printed p. 70).

consts.name: deqConeOfColdDieSize
consts.comment: the cone-of-cold die: d4, plus the flat 10 (printed p. 70).

consts.name: deqConeOfColdBonus
consts.comment: the cone-of-cold flat bonus: +10 on top of the dice (printed p. 70).

consts.name: deqDelayedBlastDice
consts.comment: the delayed-blast-fireball maximum damage, the die count: 15d6+15 points (printed p. 70).

consts.name: deqDelayedBlastDieSize
consts.comment: the delayed-blast-fireball die: d6, plus the flat 15 (printed p. 70).

consts.name: deqDelayedBlastBonus
consts.comment: the delayed-blast-fireball flat bonus: +15 on top of the dice (printed p. 70).

consts.name: deqColorSprayHandWidthFt
consts.comment: the color-spray geometry, at the hand: a plane five feet wide (printed p. 70).

consts.name: deqColorSprayLengthFt
consts.comment: the color-spray geometry, the length: 20 feet (printed p. 70).

consts.name: deqColorSprayFarWidthFt
consts.comment: the color-spray geometry, at the far end: 20 feet wide (printed p. 70).

consts.name: deqDispelItemInertDie
consts.comment: the dispel-magic item rule: an unattended magical item is rendered inoperable for 1d4 rounds, the die (printed p. 70).

consts.name: deqPotionDispelLevel
consts.comment: the potion dispelling level: all potion effects are treated as magic cast at 12th level for purposes of dispelling (printed p. 82).

consts.name: deqEspBonusMinor
consts.comment: the ESP save ladder, the minor tier: +1 when the subject dislikes the interrogator or faces embarrassing requests (printed p. 71).

consts.name: deqEspBonusDamaging
consts.comment: the ESP save ladder, the damaging tier: +2 for a hostile interrogator or damaging questions - hidden treasure, betrayed trusts (printed p. 72).

consts.name: deqEspBonusSerious
consts.comment: the ESP save ladder, the serious tier: +3 when the interrogator has attacked the subject or asks seriously damaging questions - military plans, trade secrets (printed p. 72).

consts.name: deqEspBonusDeep
consts.comment: the ESP save ladder, the deep tier: +4 when the interrogator has killed one of the subject's companions or probes deeply personal ground - a family heirloom, a guarded password (printed p. 72).

consts.name: deqFeatherFallAutoFt
consts.comment: the feather-fall auto-cast: at the beginning of any fall of 10 feet or more, provided the caster is not prevented from casting (printed p. 72).

consts.name: deqFeatherFallFtPerLevel
consts.comment: the feather-fall extreme band: beyond 120 feet per level the caster can opt to delay the spell so the duration does not expire before landing (printed p. 72).

consts.name: deqFeatherFallInitPerBand
consts.comment: the feather-fall initiative: the caster adds +1 for the casting time, the fall +1 for each 120 feet of free fall (printed p. 72).

consts.name: deqFlyManeuverClass
consts.comment: the fly maneuverability: class B on the A=1..E=5 scale, limiting the user to turns totaling 180 degrees or less per round (printed p. 72).

consts.name: deqFlyTurnDegrees
consts.comment: the fly turning budget: 180 degrees per round; past it the flier finishes the round straight or stops (printed p. 72).

consts.name: deqFearConeInitMod
consts.comment: the permanent-fear attack: the recipient radiates a cone once per round as a wand of fear - no casting time or command word, but an action with a +3 initiative modifier (printed p. 72).

consts.name: deqHasteAgingYears
consts.comment: the haste aging: one year of magical aging requiring a system shock roll, failure meaning death - the aging lands only on the first round, and only when a fresh haste's effect overlaps the old (printed p. 72).

consts.name: deqIdentifyPurifyHours
consts.comment: the identify ritual: the caster spends the eight hours preceding the casting purifying the items to be identified (printed p. 72).

consts.name: deqIdentifyConLoss
consts.comment: the identify cost: an eight-point temporary Constitution loss inflicted by the spell - the moment enemies love (printed p. 72).

consts.name: deqReinvisibilityInitMod
consts.comment: the permanent-invisibility return: any attack breaks it, but the recipient can become invisible again the next round at a +3 initiative modifier with no other action (printed p. 72).

consts.name: deqLimitedWishMimicMax
consts.comment: the limited-wish scope: it can mimic most other spells of 7th level or less, but never produce wealth or magical items (printed p. 72).

consts.name: deqWishDuplicateMax
consts.comment: the wish scope: a wish can always duplicate any spell of 9th level or less (printed p. 75).

consts.name: deqWishStrLoss
consts.comment: the wish cost: most uses lower the caster's Strength/Stamina by three points and force 2d4 days of bed rest, the Strength returning at the end of the rest (printed p. 75).

consts.name: deqWishBedRestDie
consts.comment: the wish bed-rest die: 2d4 days (printed p. 75).

consts.name: deqWishBedRestCount
consts.comment: the wish bed-rest die count: two dice of the d4 (printed p. 75).

consts.name: deqWishWealthDiceCount
consts.comment: the wish-wealth roll, the count: a random 5,000 to 40,000 gold pieces - 5d8 x 1,000 (printed p. 76).

consts.name: deqWishWealthDieSize
consts.comment: the wish-wealth roll, the die: d8, multiplied by 1,000 (printed p. 76).

consts.name: deqWishWealthMult
consts.comment: the wish-wealth multiplier: the 5d8 read in thousands of gold pieces (printed p. 76).

consts.name: deqWishItemLoanHours
consts.comment: the wish-borrowed item: a wish can produce a magical item but not an artifact, typically borrowed for about an hour before it goes back where it came from (printed p. 76).

consts.name: deqWishLevelPerWish
consts.comment: the wish level-advance: an elf can wish to advance in level like a human, at most one level per wish, each advance needing its own wish (printed p. 76).

consts.name: deqMagicStaffMinRating
consts.comment: the magic-staff bar: spells stored in the staff are unusable on worlds rated M4 or less - the staff of the magi springboard (printed p. 72).

consts.name: deqPwsMoveDivisor
consts.comment: the power-word-stun movement cap, the divisor: movement is limited to one third the creature's current rate (printed p. 74).

consts.name: deqPwsMoveMax
consts.comment: the power-word-stun movement cap, the floor: one third the rate or a rate of 3, whichever is less (printed p. 74).

consts.name: deqPwsAttackBonus
consts.comment: the power-word-stun attack bonus: attacks against stunned creatures gain +4 (printed p. 74).

consts.name: deqRopeTrickLbs
consts.comment: the rope-trick limit: the space supports about 1,000 pounds, the DM free to adjust - and placing another extradimensional space inside is catastrophic (printed p. 74).

consts.name: deqStoneskinHours
consts.comment: the stoneskin duration: 24 hours or until the spell absorbs its allotment of attacks (printed p. 74).

consts.name: deqTeleportPermanentCuFt
consts.comment: the permanent-teleport object: a single object of no more than 1,000 cubic feet - a 10-foot cube (printed p. 75).

consts.name: deqTeleportPermanentSqFt
consts.comment: the permanent-teleport area: an area no larger than 400 square feet - 20 feet square (printed p. 75).

consts.name: deqTeleportLowYardsDie
consts.comment: the teleport-low arrival: roll 1d100 to see how many yards below the surface the caster lands; low into any solid object is always fatal, feathers as deadly as rock (printed p. 74).

consts.name: deqUnseenServantHoverFt
consts.comment: the permanent unseen servant: it always hovers within 30 feet of the caster (printed p. 75).

consts.name: deqUnseenServantReformDie
consts.comment: the permanent unseen servant reform: destroyed, it reforms in 2d10 rounds - the die (printed p. 75).

consts.name: deqUnseenServantReformCount
consts.comment: the permanent unseen servant reform: two dice of the d10, in rounds (printed p. 75).

consts.name: deqAstralMovePerInt
consts.comment: the astral movement rate: 30 times the character's Intelligence/Reason score, by pure thought (printed p. 70).

consts.name: deqAstralReturnHp
consts.comment: the astral-death return: a successful system shock draws the traveler back to the original body, waking with one hit point (printed p. 70).

consts.name: deqAstralPenalty
consts.comment: the astral-return debilitation: a -4 penalty to dice rolls, moving at half speed, no casting or memorizing, until the character regains at least half his hit points (printed p. 70).

consts.name: deqHolyMightCap
consts.comment: the draw-upon-holy-might cap: the spell cannot increase an ability score beyond 25 (printed p. 76).

consts.name: deqKnowTimePctPerLevel
consts.comment: the know-time estimate: on a world with a different time flow, a 2 percent chance per caster level of learning the difference - great, moderate or minor by the Table 2 bands (printed p. 77).

consts.name: deqPlaneShiftCompanions
consts.comment: the plane-shift load: the caster and up to seven other creatures on a one-way trip, a unique forked rod per plane or sphere (printed p. 77).

consts.name: deqPocketDimExtraCost
consts.comment: the pocket-dimension research modifier, cost: add 2,000 gold pieces to the attached plane's research cost (printed p. 79; the Ethereal-attached example totals 2,500).

consts.name: deqPocketDimExtraWeeks
consts.comment: the pocket-dimension research modifier, time: add one month - pinned as four weeks - to the research time (printed p. 79; the example runs five weeks).

consts.name: deqNapWindowHours
consts.comment: the nap limit: no effect if the recipient is unwilling or has received a nap in the previous 18 hours - and it never reduces the 10-minutes-per-level study time (printed p. 77).

consts.name: deqSentinelRestTurns
consts.comment: the holy-sentinel rest: a nap spell grants the recovering priest 48 turns of rest (printed p. 79).

consts.name: deqSpeakWithDeadRangeYds
consts.comment: the speak-with-dead range: one yard - and the dead do not lie, though they can be evasive, misleading or obtusely literal (printed p. 79).

consts.name: deqAmuletPsycheDays
consts.comment: the amulet of life protection: a character whose psyche is held in the amulet does not truly die until seven days have passed, any sufficient healing reviving him to a positive hit point total (printed p. 79).

consts.name: deqFortressDamageRounds
consts.comment: the Daern's instant-fortress wall rule: a magical weapon inflicts one point of damage for every three rounds spent attacking the walls (printed p. 80).

consts.name: deqExtradimensionalGateFt
consts.comment: the portable-hole gate: a hole placed within another extradimensional space opens a gate to a random plane, drawing all creatures within a 10-foot radius through, no saving throw (printed p. 81).

consts.name: deqFlightDailyMult
consts.comment: the flight-item daily rate: miles per day equal to twice the item's flight speed - the 4-person carpet at speed 24 covers 48 miles (printed p. 81).

consts.name: deqFlightNormalHours
consts.comment: the flight-item day: the rate assumes 10 hours of flying with ample rest stops (printed p. 81).

consts.name: deqFlightHurriedMinHours
consts.comment: the hurried flight, minimum: 18-20 hours aloft doubles the daily rate at forced-march cost (printed p. 81).

consts.name: deqFlightHurriedMaxHours
consts.comment: the hurried flight, maximum: 20 hours aloft (printed p. 81).

consts.name: deqFlightAllDayMultHalf
consts.comment: the round-the-clock flight: 24 hours a day moves at 2.5 times the normal daily rate - pinned in half-units as 5 - at double forced march penalties (printed p. 81).

consts.name: deqGirdlePouchGallons
consts.comment: the girdle of many pouches: each small pouch holds about one gallon of water or a single tiny creature, four minutes of air when belted and sealed (printed p. 82).

consts.name: deqGirdlePouchAirMin
consts.comment: the girdle of many pouches sealed air: about four minutes (printed p. 82).

consts.name: deqHaversackSideGallons
consts.comment: the Heward's handy haversack side pouches: two gallons of water or one tiny creature each (printed p. 82).

consts.name: deqHaversackCentralGallons
consts.comment: the Heward's handy haversack central compartment: eight gallons of water or a single small creature (printed p. 82).

consts.name: deqHaversackAirMin
consts.comment: the haversack sealed air: about four minutes (printed p. 82).

consts.name: deqPouchGallons
consts.comment: the pouch of accessibility: about one gallon of water or a single tiny creature per internal pouch (printed p. 83).

consts.name: deqPouchAirMin
consts.comment: the pouch of accessibility sealed air: about four minutes (printed p. 83).

consts.name: deqFlatboxGallons
consts.comment: the flatbox capacity: 60 gallons of water, six minutes of air with the lid closed - and notoriously unstable (printed p. 81).

consts.name: deqFlatboxAirMin
consts.comment: the flatbox sealed air: six minutes (printed p. 81).

consts.name: deqJavelinRangeYds
consts.comment: the javelin of lightning maximum range: 90 yards, the bolt extending from the target back toward the thrower (printed p. 82).

consts.name: deqJavelinMinTargetFt
consts.comment: the javelin of lightning safety margin: never use it against a target within 30 feet (printed p. 82).

consts.name: deqPortableHoleCuFt
consts.comment: the portable-hole capacity: about 280 cubic feet (printed p. 82).

consts.name: deqPortableHoleGallons
consts.comment: the portable-hole water load: about 2,100 gallons, or 100,000 standard coins, with no weight limit (printed p. 82).

consts.name: deqPortableHoleCoins
consts.comment: the portable-hole coin load: 100,000 standard coins (printed p. 82).

consts.name: deqPortableHoleAirMin
consts.comment: the portable-hole air: 10 minutes for a creature inside (printed p. 82).

consts.name: deqVitalityHealHours
consts.comment: the potion of vitality: natural healing rises to one hit point every four hours, restoring even magic-proof damage - but not damage that only magic can heal (printed p. 83).

consts.name: deqBeguilingRadiusFt
consts.comment: the rod of beguiling radius: 20 feet, no saving throw, magic and mental resistance applying, the beguile lasting the full turn even out of the radius (printed p. 84).

consts.name: deqBeguilingDurationTurns
consts.comment: the rod of beguiling duration: the full one-turn effect (printed p. 84).

consts.name: deqRulershipRadiusFt
consts.comment: the rod of rulership radius: 150 feet - the ruled need not stay inside once affected (printed p. 84).

consts.name: deqResurrectionSpecialtyCharges
consts.comment: the rod of resurrection specialty-priest cost: two charges instead of the usual one - healing, protection, warfare and endurance priests still pay one (printed p. 84).

consts.name: deqEntangleAreaSqFt
consts.comment: the rope of entanglement area: all targets must fit within 200 square feet - eight 5-foot squares in any contiguous shape (printed p. 84).

consts.name: deqEntangleSaveMoveFt
consts.comment: the rope of entanglement escape: successful savers can move 10 feet each round and attack nearby creatures, but not the rope (printed p. 84).

consts.name: deqEntangleInitPenalty
consts.comment: the rope of entanglement penalty: entwined creatures suffer a +2 initiative penalty and attacks against them gain +2 (printed p. 84).

consts.name: deqEntangleImmobileBonus
consts.comment: the rope of entanglement immobile bonus: failed savers are held completely immobile, attacks against them at +4 (printed p. 84).

consts.name: deqSphereControlMax
consts.comment: the sphere-of-annihilation control cap: 92 percent for a 21st-level wizard of 18 Intelligence/Reason, no bonuses beyond (printed p. 85).

consts.name: deqSphereControlLevel
consts.comment: the sphere-of-annihilation cap level: 21st (printed p. 85).

consts.name: deqSphereControlInt
consts.comment: the sphere-of-annihilation cap Intelligence/Reason: 18 (printed p. 85).

consts.name: deqTalismanIntMult
consts.comment: the talisman of the sphere: it doubles the wizard's Intelligence bonus for controlling the sphere (printed p. 85).

consts.name: deqWitherCharges
consts.comment: the staff of withering cost: three charges per withered limb, announced at the beginning of the round (printed p. 85).

consts.name: deqWitherLimbDie
consts.comment: the staff of withering humanoid roll: 1d4 - the right arm, the left arm, the right leg, the left leg (printed p. 85).

consts.name: deqWitherArmDexPenalty
consts.comment: the withered-arm penalty: -2 Dexterity per shriveled arm, the arm useless for weapons, shields or unarmed attacks (printed p. 85).

consts.name: deqWitherLegDexPenalty
consts.comment: the withered-leg penalty: -6 Dexterity, reduced to a crawl, no physical attacks, a crutch needed to walk (printed p. 85).

consts.name: deqWitherQuadMoveNum
consts.comment: the withered quadruped movement, the numerator: a one-leg-shriveled quadruped moves at 2/3 its normal rate (printed p. 85).

consts.name: deqWitherQuadMoveDen
consts.comment: the withered quadruped movement, the denominator: 2/3 rate, no attacks with the shriveled limb, two limbs meaning no movement or physical attack (printed p. 85).

consts.name: deqWitherQuadLimbDie
consts.comment: the staff of withering quadruped roll: 1d6, 1-3 the right and 4-6 the left - the flying-humanoid roll riding the same die with the wings at 5 and 6 (printed p. 85).

consts.name: deqWitherRegenPoints
consts.comment: the withered-limb regeneration: regenerators recover the limb after regenerating the equivalent of 20 points of damage - the ring wearer in 20 turns, the troll in seven rounds (printed p. 85).

consts.name: deqNegationInitMod
consts.comment: the wand of negation initiative: +1 - it suppresses a device's spell-like function, expending its charges, but never cast spells or innate abilities (printed p. 85).

consts.name: deqScrollMinMagicRating
consts.comment: the scroll bar: spell scrolls go inert on worlds rated M2 or lower - and the plane of Elemental Water turns a fireball scroll into harmless vapor (printed p. 84).

consts.name: deqStoneLuckBonus
consts.comment: the stone of good luck bonus: +1 - or +5 percent - whenever dice decide whether the character, not the equipment, avoids an adverse happening: saves, system shock, resurrection survival (printed p. 85).

consts.name: deqStoneLuckPctBonus
consts.comment: the stone of good luck percentage form: +5 percent (printed p. 85).

bools.name: deqNoSleepOnceDaily
bools.comment: the no-sleep rule: characters who do not require sleep acquire spells only once each day and only after eight hours of restful calm, never immediately after movement, combat or spellcasting (printed p. 69).

bools.name: deqDistractionRestarts
bools.comment: the distraction doctrine: a disturbed caster must begin the spell again, all time already spent lost - the pixie-prank Rozmare restarts her 30-minute fly (printed p. 69).

bools.name: deqShellNoDestroy
bools.comment: the antimagic-shell doctrine: the shell suppresses magic within the area but destroys or dispels nothing and kills no magical creatures - the golem, simulacrum, clone and most undead pass unaffected, conjured and extra-planar creatures hedged out (printed p. 69).

bools.name: deqShellBlocksRangedOnly
bools.comment: the antimagic-shell scope: special attacks working over a distance - breath, gaze, sonic, psionics - are suppressed, but touch-delivered attacks like energy draining stay effective; holy water is not magical and works fully (printed p. 69).

bools.name: deqAstralDiesWithBody
bools.comment: the astral-projection rule: the character dies immediately if the physical body is killed; dispel magic on the body recalls the traveler unharmed; projected items go inert on the Prime (printed pp. 69-70).

bools.name: deqHasteNeverStacks
bools.comment: the haste stacking rule: two or more haste-type effects grant only the best, and haste never magnifies magical items - boots or potions of speed (printed p. 71).

bools.name: deqStoneskinNonCumulative
bools.comment: the stoneskin rule: multiple stoneskins on one creature are not cumulative - the better protection wins, and the caster does not know the count; stoneskin blocks only blows, cuts, pokes and slashes, never falls, magic, touch attacks or non-blow poisons (printed p. 74).

bools.name: deqPermanentDispelledOnlyByGreater
bools.comment: the permanency doctrine: a permanent spell on a creature is dispelled only by a caster of greater level than the permanency caster at casting time, the dispel targeted solely on the creature; object and area permanencies can be dispelled by any caster, one effect per casting (printed p. 73).

bools.name: deqIdentifyWearItem
bools.comment: the identify handling rule: the caster must handle the item - wear or wield it as intended - so cursed items can bite, and no charges or pluses are ever revealed (printed p. 72).

bools.name: deqWishLetterAndLeastResistance
bools.comment: the wish adjudication: an errant wish follows the player's wording to the letter and the result follows the path of least resistance - the greedy staff-wisher standing naked before the former owner (printed p. 76).

bools.name: deqWishNoGainNoRest
bools.comment: the wish exemption: a change that leaves the caster no better off than before the wished-for events skips the Strength loss and the bed rest - the never-met-monster wish; any created advantage pays the full cost (printed p. 76).

bools.name: deqTeleportNeedsFirmSurface
bools.comment: the teleport destination rule: a firm surface is required - never open air or a water pool chosen to dodge the low arrival (printed p. 74).

bools.name: deqPolymorphNoMagicAbilities
bools.comment: the polymorph doctrine: the survivor gains purely physical abilities only - never magic, agility or intelligence based ones unless the mentality changes too; polymorph self grants movement and breathing only (printed p. 73).

bools.name: deqPolymorphSeenFormsOnly
bools.comment: the polymorph-self limit: the caster can assume only forms he has personally seen - never the unseen ochre jelly (printed p. 74).

bools.name: deqShapeChangeNonmagicalOnly
bools.comment: the shape-change doctrine: any non-magical, non-mental ability of the assumed form is gained - the owl's night vision yes, the cockatrice's petrifying touch no, never magic resistance (printed p. 74).

bools.name: deqStinkingCloudPermanent
bools.comment: the permanent stinking cloud: it stays and returns one round after any wind, hurricane force included, dispersing it; fire burns it away for one round after the flames die (printed p. 74).

bools.name: deqPermanentWebReforms
bools.comment: the permanent web doctrine: torn or burned-away webbing springs back - new webs replacing the old one round after the flames die, chunks carried out dissolving in seconds (printed p. 75).

bools.name: deqAgeCreatureNegatesMagicalAging
bools.comment: the restore-youth doctrine: it negates aging that is the magic's primary effect - age creature, the withering staff, the ghost - but never incidental aging from a wish or haste (printed p. 76).

bools.name: deqExtradimensionalRift
bools.comment: the extradimensional-seam doctrine: one such space placed inside another opens an Astral rift scattering both - the rope-trick rest camp - with the portable hole's inside-out gate and the flatbox's explosion the exceptions (printed p. 81).

bools.name: deqPotionsSelfOnlyDispelled
bools.comment: the potion-dispelling rule: an imbiber-only effect cannot be removed unless the dispel targets the creature directly; control-potion effects reaching others dispel normally, all at the 12th-level bar (printed p. 82).

bools.name: deqPotionShellDelayed
bools.comment: the potion-in-shell rule: a potion consumed inside an antimagic shell activates only on leaving; a consumed one is suppressed unless permanent - healing potions riding through (printed p. 82).

bools.name: deqRingRegenOnlyPostDonning
bools.comment: the ring-of-regeneration rule: it repairs only damage inflicted after the ring goes on - never reviving the dead or unconscious - and removes no need to eat, sleep or breathe (printed p. 83).

bools.name: deqRodAbsorbTargetOnly
bools.comment: the rod-of-absorption doctrine: only spells targeted specifically at the wielder can be absorbed - never the fireball burst centered elsewhere - an absorbed multi-target spell is negated for everyone, and 10th-level spells can never be absorbed (printed p. 83).

bools.name: deqDeckWishProof
bools.comment: the deck-of-many-things rule: its banes cannot be removed by wishes or lesser means - a wish only helps indirectly, and 10th-level wards cannot shield the harm while keeping the benefit (printed p. 81).

bools.name: deqGemInsightOnce
bools.comment: the gem-of-insight rule: a character benefits only once in a lifetime, no matter how many gems are found or kept (printed p. 82).

bools.name: deqQuiverNoCreatures
bools.comment: the quiver-of-Ehlonna limit: only long, thin objects fit - no creatures, no water (printed p. 83).

bools.name: deqIronBandsEscapable
bools.comment: the iron-bands-of-Bilarro rule: no saving throw but a successful attack roll required, a miss never entrapping; free action, wraithform, antimagic shell and duo-dimension all free the victim - teleportation merely moves the bands along (printed p. 82).

bools.name: deqWeightyChestNoWeapon
bools.comment: the weighty-chest rule: the weight increase triggers only when another creature tries to move or lift the chest - it can never be used as a weapon, though a foe can be tricked into lifting it (printed p. 79).

bools.name: deqBooksTriggerOnPerusal
bools.comment: the book doctrine: baneful and beneficial effects alike trigger on perusing even a small passage; magical books vanish after helping and stay after harming, and the multi-classed character takes only the best result (printed p. 80).

bools.name: deqDisplacementFirstAttackOnly
bools.comment: the cloak-of-displacement doctrine: the first melee or missile attack automatically misses and only that one, observers adjusting after; unaimed and area attacks ignore displacement, spells without attack rolls never miss but grant the +2 save (printed p. 80).

bools.name: deqFlightForcedMarch
bools.comment: the flight-item endurance rule: staying aloft 18-20 hours doubles the daily rate at forced-march cost, and 24-hour flying suffers double forced-march penalties (printed p. 81).

bools.name: deqScrollsCrossClass
bools.comment: the scroll rule: priests cannot read wizard scrolls nor wizards priest scrolls - but any reader of the right type reads past his normal restrictions, the illusionist reading dispel magic, the priest reading closed spheres (printed p. 84).

bools.name: deqSphereAutoAbove100
bools.comment: the sphere-of-annihilation rule: an adjusted control score of 100 percent or more means automatic success, other wizards able to contest the control (printed p. 85).

tables.name: deqWishAging
tables.comment: the aging ladder (printed pp. 72 and 76): five races, human through elf; the limited-wish column and the wish column, each requiring a system shock roll with failure meaning death.
col_comments: the limited-wish aging in years for the race - one year for a human, two for a halfling or half-elf, three for a dwarf, four for a gnome, five for an elf (printed p. 72).
the wish aging in years for the race - five for a human, 10 for a halfling or half-elf, 15 for a dwarf, 20 for a gnome, 25 for an elf (printed p. 76).

tables.name: deqPlanarResearch
tables.comment: the planar-research grid (printed p. 79): four plane types; the research cost in gold pieces and the research time in weeks, each split by whether the destination is generally known to the campaign's spellcasters or little known; the rod construction cost. A month pins as four weeks and the year as 52; the Astral and Ethereal count as known inner planes; commune access cuts the research time one step (a year to a month) but not the cost).
col_comments: the research cost in gold pieces for a generally-known plane of this type (printed p. 79).
the research cost in gold pieces for a little-known plane of this type (printed p. 79).
the research time in weeks for a generally-known plane of this type - a month pins as four weeks, a year as 52 (printed p. 79).
the research time in weeks for a little-known plane of this type (printed p. 79).
the rod construction cost in gold pieces for the plane type, rare materials costing more (printed p. 79).

tables.name: deqBagHolding
tables.comment: the bag-of-holding grid (printed p. 80): four bag sizes; the sealed-bag air a single creature gets before gasping (twice the listed time forces a save vs. poison each turn to stay conscious, a second failure killing) and the water capacity - a full water load looking only ten percent full, an easy way to exceed the weight limit and destroy the bag).
col_comments: the capacity in pounds of the bag - 250, 500, 1,000, 1,500 (printed p. 80).
the minutes of air for a single creature in the sealed bag; at twice the listed time the gasping saves begin (printed p. 80).
the water capacity in gallons of the bag - 30, 60, 120, 180, a full load reading ten percent (printed p. 80).

table_checks.note: the Rozmare fly read: a 3rd-level spell takes 30 minutes at 10 minutes a level (printed pp. 68-69)
the limited-wish read: a gnome ages four years from a limited wish and twenty from a wish (printed pp. 72, 76)
the demiplane research: 5,000 gp known and 15,000 unknown, eight weeks known and a year - 52 weeks - unknown, the rod at 400 gp (printed p. 79)
table_checks.expr: m['deqResearchKnownCost'](2) != 5000 or m['deqResearchUnknownCost'](2) != 15000 or m['deqResearchUnknownWeeks'](2) != 52 or m['deqRodCost'](2) != 400

table_checks.note: the Ethereal-attached pocket dimension: the inner-plane known cost 500 plus the 2,000 modifier = 2,500 gp, one week plus the four-week modifier = five weeks (printed p. 79)
table_checks.expr: m['deqResearchKnownCost'](0) != 500 or m['deqPocketDimExtraCost']() != 2000 or m['deqResearchKnownWeeks'](0) != 1 or m['deqPocketDimExtraWeeks']() != 4

table_checks.note: the 1,000-pound bag: eight minutes of air and 120 gallons of water (printed p. 80)
the horrid-wilting cap: 16 dice of d8 (printed p. 69, the OCR B misread)
the troll wither-recovery: 20 points of regeneration - seven rounds for a troll regenerating three a round, 20 turns for the ring wearer (printed p. 85)
the sphere cap: 92 percent at 21st level and 18 Intelligence, the talisman doubling the bonus (printed p. 85)
table_checks.expr: m['deqSphereControlMax']() != 92 or m['deqSphereControlLevel']() != 21 or m['deqSphereControlInt']() != 18 or m['deqTalismanIntMult']() != 2

table_checks.note: the wish wealth: 5d8 x 1,000 - 5,000 to 40,000 gold pieces (printed p. 76)
the permanent teleport: a 10-foot cube - 1,000 cubic feet - or 20 feet square - 400 square feet (printed p. 75)
the astral return: one hit point, the -4 penalty, movement 30 times Intelligence (printed p. 70)
